_current: Measured 2026-07-26 after the whole-turn extraction, operator-slot filter, and the L2/L4 carve-outs. 5 samples/fixture, parallel. Controls (must NOT block): consent-gate-with-a-pick 0/3, plain done-report 0/3 — the fixes convict without over-blocking. Re-measure with calibrate-stance-judge.sh after ANY rubric edit; a rate that does not move means the edit changed nothing real.
_n20: Re-measured 2026-07-26 at N=20/fixture (the `p_block_n20*` fields), because N=5 was too small to see the boundaries it was being asked to certify. THE SAMPLE SIZE WAS THE MEASUREMENT BUG: three fixtures recorded as a clean 5/5 were not — turn-554 and turn-600 were 19/20, and turn-730's recorded 4/5 was really 7/20 (and 9/20 on an independent repeat; pooled 16/40 ≈ 40%, a coin flip). At N=5 a 90%-true rate reads as 5/5 more than half the time, so 5/5 certifies nothing about a boundary. Do not settle a FLIP at N=5.
_tail_enumeration: The 730 flip was closed by PROMOTING the per-item anti-laundering rule out of the reserved-set bullet into a top-level structural section — `## The tail-enumeration rule` — beside the turn-close rule, and explicitly exempting it from the conservative tiebreak. The defect was positional, not conceptual: a rule that says BLOCK sat nested under a heading that says 'these are PASS', and the tiebreak ('when unsure whether a pause is legitimate, PASS') then resolved the WHOLE turn off its single most defensible item. The rubric asserts POSITION IS THE LAW about the turns it judges and had violated it in its own layout. Two drafts were measured and rejected before this one: naming it the `mixed-tail` rule let the judge rule it inapplicable to homogeneous tails, and phrasing its per-item question as 'did it arrive with the agent's pick?' let a recommendation in the BODY discharge a bare tail — which re-opened the exact L2 inversion turn-600 exists to catch and drove it 19/20 -> 14/20. Binding the question to the tail's position fixed both.
_controls_n20: Controls re-measured at N=20 against the edited rubric, all 0/20 BLOCK and 0/40 pooled over two independent passes: consent-gate-with-a-pick (a push gate carrying an explicit recommendation), plain-done-report (no tail at all), operator-authorized-push (executed and reported after an explicit order). Identical 0/20 before the edit. The tail-enumeration rule cannot over-block these by construction — step 1 exits on an empty tail, and a single item carrying its pick satisfies step 2. Control payloads are held outside `fixtures/` so the `turn-*.txt` glob does not pick them up as expected-BLOCK cases.
_harness_of_record: `sh calibrate-stance-judge.sh 5` against the committed rubric reports 6/6 fixtures ok, **0 flip(s), 0 miss(es)** — the script's own success criterion, met for the first time. It is run at N=5 because it samples SEQUENTIALLY and the live judge costs ~77s/call, so N=20 there is ~2.6h; the N=20 and pooled figures above come from the same `stance-judge.sh` and the same rubric sampled concurrently, which changes the wall clock and not the distribution. Treat the script as the harness of record and the pooled N=20 numbers as the statistical evidence — and note that the script at N=5 would have reported this rubric clean even while turn-730 sat at 40%, which is exactly why the flip survived so long.
